link_power_management_states.description: PHY active, ESM in Op, cyclic exchange running. PHY draws ~250 mW per 100BASE-TX port; ESC core draws 300-1500 mW depending on vendor + features.
Port has no link partner. ESC port automatically loops; PHY backs off to low-power link-pulse mode.
Power-up sequence — PHY auto-negotiation, ESC SII load, AL Status = Init.

fields.low_power_modes_summary: EtherCAT does not define mandated PHY low-power states beyond IEEE 802.3 (Power-Down via MII Control register BMCR bit 11). Energy-Efficient Ethernet (IEEE 802.3az) Low-Power Idle (LPI) is generally NOT used by EtherCAT MainDevices because LPI wake delay is incompatible with sub-millisecond cycle times. EtherCAT P delivers 24 V DC US + UP power alongside data on the same cable, but does not introduce new low-power states.
fields.device_states_d0_d3_analog: Not applicable — EtherCAT is a network protocol, not a PCI Express endpoint; no D0/D3 power-management states.
fields.auxiliary_power_for_wake_on_lan: Not specified — EtherCAT does not define a Wake-on-LAN mechanism. Standard SubDevices remain powered as long as the application requires.
fields.pause_flow_control_summary: EtherCAT does NOT use IEEE 802.3x PAUSE frames. Flow control is implicit: the MainDevice originates frames at a deterministic cycle rate; SubDevices process on-the-fly without buffering; no link congestion can occur because there is no shared collision domain (every link is a dedicated point-to-point full-duplex 100BASE-TX or 100BASE-FX wire).

rails.name: US (System / Sensor / Electronics)
rails.purpose: Logic + sensor power; coupled on twisted pair 1+2

rails.name: UP (Peripheral / Actuator)
rails.purpose: Actuator drive power; coupled on twisted pair 3+6

ethercat_p_power_summary.coupling: ETG-specified magnetics combine 24V DC power with 100BASE-TX differential signaling on the same 4-conductor cable.

fields.notes: EtherCAT MainDevice power consumption is a property of the host PC / industrial controller, not of EtherCAT itself. SubDevice ESC consumption is typically 0.3-1.5 W; PHYs add another ~250 mW per active 100BASE-TX port. Local µC consumption depends on application I/O complexity.
